sentences.text: Muttaburrasaurus was a large dinosaur approximately 8 meters long with an estimated body mass of 2.8 metric tons.
This animal is comparable in size to large T. rex specimens and bull African bush elephants, making it the largest ornithischian known to retain premaxillary teeth.
The skull of Muttaburrasaurus was long and featured a triangular cross-section when viewed from above.
The femur of the holotype specimen measures 1015 mm in length.
Muttaburrasaurus had a long and wide foot equipped with four toes.
The 'Dunluce Skull' (specimen QM F14921) was discovered in 1987 by John Stewart-Moore and 14-year-old Robert Walker on Dunluce Station.
Reconstructed skeleton casts of Muttaburrasaurus, sponsored by Kellogg Company, are displayed at museums including the Queensland Museum, Flinders Discovery Centre, and the Australian Museum.
The dinosaur was named after Muttaburra, the location in Queensland, Australia where its fossils were discovered.
The species was formally named in 1981 by Bartholomai and Ralph Molnar, giving it the specific name langdoni to honor its discoverer.
The holotype specimen QM F6140 was discovered in the Mackunda Formation.
Muttaburrasaurus is the second most completely known non-avian dinosaur from Australia, following Kunbarrasaurus.
Muttaburrasaurus possessed very powerful jaws equipped with shearing teeth designed for cutting.
In Muttaburrasaurus, replacement teeth grew directly under the functional teeth with only a single erupted generation, precluding a chewing motion.
The teeth show eleven low ridges instead of a main crest.
This dental arrangement may have been an adaptation for feeding on tough vegetation such as cycads.
It is debated whether Muttaburrasaurus was capable of quadrupedal movement, though recent studies suggest it adopted a bipedal posture similar to rhabdodonts.
Quadrupedal locomotion in Muttaburrasaurus likely occurred only when moving slowly or while stationary to browse on foliage.
A 2026 reanalysis suggests Muttaburrasaurus was a selective feeder with a strong sense of smell due to its narrow snout.
Muttaburrasaurus is classified within the unranked family Rhabdodontomorpha and is considered a rabdodontomorph ornithopod dinosaur.
Muttaburrasaurus has been classified in various analyses as a member of Rhabdodontomorpha, but recent research suggests it may belong to the basal clade Elasmaria.
Molnar originally assigned Muttaburrasaurus to Iguanodontidae, but later authors suggested it belonged to basal groups like Camptosauridae, Dryosauridae, or Hypsilophodontidae.
Muttaburrasaurus lived during the middle Cretaceous period, approximately 112 to 98.6 million years ago, in the Albian and Cenomanian stages.
Muttaburrasaurus lived from 106.3 to 93.9 million years ago during the Albian to Cenomanian stages.
It is debated whether the hollow bulge on the snout was a resonating chamber, with later research concluding it was part of an elongated premaxilla.
It is debated whether Muttaburrasaurus was an omnivore that ate carrion, a hypothesis proposed by Molnar in 1981 but later revised.
